title: Gradual activation lattice with human-in-the-loop checkpoints for Optimize recommendations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Implement a gradual, lattice-style activation pipeline that applies Optimize (batching/caching) recommendations with operator checkpoints and automated telemetry gates. The goal is to safely reduce per-token cost while bounding latency and quality regressions. The lattice is a directed activation graph of tiers (pilot -> narrow canary -> regional pulse -> broad rollout) where each transition requires a combination of automated checks (telemetry thresholds, simulated traffic probes, deterministic replay) and a human-in-the-loop acknowledgment for high-risk transitions. Key aspects:

- Motivation: current manual adoption of Optimize recs is slow and inconsistent across tenants. We need a deterministic, auditable, and reversible activation flow that reduces ops burden while keeping risk low for critical customers.
- Success metrics: reduce median cost-per-token by X% for adopters who accept recs, <5% tail latency regression vs baseline, no more than 0.5% increase in user-visible quality regressions on monitored prompts, and <1 hour mean time to rollback for failed activations.
- Scope: batching and prefix/KV caching configuration changes suggested by Optimize. Does NOT include model quantization changes or infra-size adjustments (separate project).
- Architecture: controller service will manage per-tenant activation state, emit deterministic plan steps, run automated probes (synthetic traffic + shadow replay), and hold transitions in a pending state until operator ack or automated gate passes. A sidecar admission webhook enforces active config only after commit and tags commits with rollout metadata for tracing.
- Observability & instrumentation: expand Console to show per-activation telemetry (cost delta, qps, p50/p95 latency, eval-quality delta by prompt set), link directly to PR diffs and the request traces that contributed to gate failures. All activation artifacts must be stored in the customer audit log.
- Safety: implement two-tier rollback: fast halt (stop progression to next tier) and full revert (atomic revert of config with circuit-breaker to block re-apply for a configurable cooldown). Reverts must notify operators and create a follow-up postmortem checklist.

Trade-offs considered: fully automated autocommit is faster but risks undetected quality drift; heavy operator gating increases cycle time and burden. We chose a hybrid lattice with automated low-risk transitions and operator approval for transitions that touch >20% of a tenant's traffic or when simulated-eval deltas exceed thresholds.

Open questions:
- Default thresholds for quality delta and cost floor (propose: cost delta >= 5% AND quality delta <= 0.25% for automated promotion).
- How to surface correlated regressions across prompt cohorts vs noisy single-prompt flukes.

Deliverables:
- Controller microservice, rollout metadata schema, and admission sidecar integration.
- Console dashboards & activation detail page.
- Operator runbook and an improveable checklist for approvals and post-rollback analysis.
- E2E tests including synthetic traffic harness and canary-replay tool.
acceptance_criteria: Controller manages activation state and can pause/resume per-tenant flows
Automated telemetry gates defined and enforced (latency, cost, quality eval) with configurable thresholds
Human operator can view pending transitions in Console and either approve or reject with a mandatory rationale
Rollback path exists that reverts config within target MTTR and blocks immediate re-apply during cooldown
Activation events, approvals, and reverts are logged to customer audit trail and linked to traces/PRs
E2E tests simulate rollout across pilot->canary->regional->global lanes and validate rollback behavior
